{{nihongo|'''Imaki-Aosaka-Inami-Ikegami Shrine'''|今城青坂稲実池上神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in Shibo, Kamisato Town, Kodama District, Saitama Prefecture, along the {{ill|Karasu River (Gunma)|ceb|Karasu Gawa (suba sa Hapon, lat 36,27, long 139,17)|fa|رود کاراسو (گونما)|fr|Karasu-gawa|ja|烏川 (利根川水系)|lfn|Rio Karasu (Gunma)|ru|Карасу (приток Тоне)|qid=Q3915532|lt=Karasu River}}, a tributary of the {{ill|Tone River|ar|توني (نهر)|arz|نهر تونى|be|Тонэ|bg|Тоне (река)|ca|Riu Tone|cs|Tone|de|Tone (Fluss)|eo|Tone (rivero)|es|Río Tone|eu|Tone ibaia|fa|تونه‌گاوا|fi|Tonejoki|fr|Tone-gawa|he|טונה (נהר)|hi|टोन नदी|hu|Tone (folyó, Japán)|id|Sungai Tone|it|Tone (fiume)|ja|利根川|ko|도네강|lt|Tonė|nl|Tone (Japanse rivier)|no|Tone (elv)|pl|Tone (rzeka)|pt|Rio Tone|ru|Тоне (река)|simple|Tone River|sv|Tonegawa|th|แม่น้ำโทเนะ|tr|Tone Nehri|uk|Тоне (річка)|vi|Sông Tone (Nhật Bản)|wuu|利根川|zh|利根川|qid=Q177452}}. The enshrined deities are {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|ja|祓戸大神|zh|祓戶大神|qid=Q11588504|lt=Ibukido-nushi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Toyouke-hime|abstract|Q2983724|bcl|Toyoukebime|es|Toyouke Ōmikami|fr|Toyouke Ōmikami|ja|トヨウケビメ|kk|Тоёукэ бимэ|ru|Тоёукэ бимэ|simple|Toyōke Ōmikami|sv|Toyouke Ōmikami|tok|jan sewi suli Tojoke|zh|豐宇氣毘賣神|qid=Q2983724}}. {{Citation needed range|It is considered a candidate shrine (ronsha) of the Engishiki-listed “Imaki Aoyasaka Inami Ikegami Shrine” of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}{{ill|Kami district|Q11634927|qid=Q11634927}}, and its former shrine rank was Prefectural Shrine|date=February 2025}}. {{nihongo|'''Imaki-Aosaka-Inami-Ikegami Shrine'''|今城青坂稲実池上神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

== History ==
A clan of immigrant origin with advanced rice-cultivation technology enshrined the rice deity “Toyouke-hime-no-Mikoto” as their tutelary deity and founded the shrine in Wadō 4 (711) in Shibo along the Karasu River. <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒">Shrine noticeboard, “The 62nd Ise Grand Shrine Shikinen Sengū Commemoration: History of Imaki Aoyasaka Inami Ikegami Shrine”</ref>  

Later, as the immigrant clan declined, the shrine fell into ruin, {{Citation needed range|the shrine name “Imaki Aoyasaka Inami Ikegami Shrine” was lost|date=February 2025}} and it came to be called “Inari Shrine.” During the {{ill|Genkō (1331–1334)|de|Genkō|fa|گنکو (۳۴-۱۳۳۱)|fr|Ère Genkō (deuxième)|ia|Genko|ja|元弘|ko|겐코 (1331년)|ru|Гэнко|simple|Genkō (era)|sr|Генко (друга ера)|sv|Genkō|tr|Genkō (ikinci)|zh|元弘|qid=Q1194556}} era (1331–1334), {{ill|Nitta Yoshisada|Q1328796|qid=Q1328796}} rebuilt it as protection against the northeast (kimon) for Kanakubo Castle. At this time, for apotropaic purposes, the Haraedo deity “{{ill|Haraedo no Kami|ja|祓戸大神|zh|祓戶大神|qid=Q11588504|lt=Ibukido-nushi-no-Mikoto}}” is thought to have been enshrined.
In {{ill|Engen|de|Engen (Ära)|fa|انگن (دوره)|fr|Ère Engen|ia|Engen|ja|延元|ko|엔겐|ru|Энгэн|simple|Engen|sr|Енген (ера)|sv|Engen|tr|Engen (dönem)|zh|延元|qid=Q1194159}} 3 ({{ill|1338|ab|1338|af|1338|als|1338|am|1338 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1338|ar|1338|ary|1338|ast|1338|avk|1338|az|1338|azb|۱۳۳۸ (میلادی)|be|1338|be_x_old|1338|bg|1338|bn|১৩৩৮|bpy|মারি ১৩৩৮|br|1338|bs|1338.|ca|1338|cdo|1338 nièng|ceb|1338|ckb|١٣٣٨|crh|1338|cs|1338|cv|1338|cy|1338|da|1338|de|1338|diq|1338|el|1338|eml|1338|eo|1338|es|1338|et|1338|eu|1338|fa|۱۳۳۸ (میلادی)|fi|1338|fo|1338|fr|1338|frr|1338|fy|1338|ga|1338|gan|1338年|gcr|1338|gd|1338|gl|1338|he|1338|hi|१३३८|hr|1338.|ht|1338 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1338|hy|1338|id|1338|ilo|1338|io|1338|is|1338|it|1338|ja|1338年|jv|1338|ka|1338|kaa|1338|kk|1338 жыл|ko|1338년|la|1338|lb|1338|lij|1338|lmo|1338|lt|1338 m.|lv|1338. gads|mai|१३३८|map_bms|1338|mdf|1338|mg|1338|mhr|1338|mi|1338|min|1338|mk|1338|mr|इ.स. १३३८|mrj|1338 и|ms|1338|my|၁၃၃၈|mzn|۱۳۳۸|nah|1338|nap|1338|nds|1338|new|सन् १३३८|nl|1338|nn|1338|no|1338|nrm|1338|nso|1338|oc|1338|or|୧୩୩୮|os|1338-æм аз|pl|1338|pnb|1338|pt|1338|qu|1338|ro|1338|ru|1338 год|rue|1338|sa|१३३८|sah|1338|scn|1338|sd|1338ع|se|1338|sh|1338.|shn|1338|simple|1338|sk|1338|sl|1338|smn|1338|sq|1338|sr|1338|su|1338|sv|1338|sw|1338|tg|Соли 1338|th|พ.ศ. 1881|tk|1338|tl|1338|tly|1338|tr|1338|tt|1338 ел|uk|1338|ur|1338ء|uz|1338|vec|1338|vi|1338|wa|1338|war|1338|wuu|1338年|xmf|1338|zh|1338年|zh_min_nan|1338 nî|zh_yue|1338年|qid=Q6044}}), Tokiko Yoshimune became lord of Kanakubo and prayed for victory in battle.
In {{ill|Jōji|es|Jōji|fa|جوجی (دوره)|fr|Ère Jōji|ja|貞治|ko|조지 (난보쿠초 시대)|ru|Дзёдзи|simple|Jōji|sr|Џоџи|sv|Jōji|th|โจจิ|tr|Jōji|zh|貞治|qid=Q1146153}} 2 ({{ill|1363|Q6176|qid=Q6176}}), when {{ill|Uesugi Noriaki|Q11359188|qid=Q11359188}} became {{ill|Kantō Kanrei|Q5367751|qid=Q5367751}} and lord of Kanakubo, he prayed for peace along the borders in {{ill|Ōan|Q1146245|qid=Q1146245}} 1 ({{ill|1368|Q6207|qid=Q6207}}). <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒" />

In {{ill|Daiei (era)|Q1193564|qid=Q1193564}} 4 ({{ill|1524|Q6309|qid=Q6309}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Saitō Morimitsu}} became lord of Kanakubo Castle and, like the Nitta clan, made the shrine the castle’s guardian deity. <ref name="池上神社">Shrine noticeboard “Ikegami Shrine” (installed by Kamisato Town, Saitama Prefecture; March 1986)</ref>
In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 10 ({{ill|1582|Q6719|qid=Q6719}}) June, {{ill|Kami district|Q11634927|qid=Q11634927}} of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}} became a battlefield in the “{{ill|Battle of Kanagawa|Q1058786|qid=Q1058786}}” between {{ill|Takigawa Kazumasu|Q953624|qid=Q953624}}, a retainer of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}, and the Hōjō forces led by {{ill|Hōjō Ujimasa|Q736948|qid=Q736948}}. The shrine buildings were destroyed by fire. <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒"/>
In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19 ({{ill|1590|Q6764|qid=Q6764}}) January, Kawakubo Nobutoshi became lord of Kanakubo, and in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19 ({{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}}) he rebuilt the shrine buildings that had burned down and donated sacred rice fields. Kawakubo Nobutoshi was the son of “{{ill|Takeda Nobuzane|Q11546097|qid=Q11546097}},” younger brother of {{ill|Takeda Shingen|Q276404|qid=Q276404}}.
In {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 7 ({{ill|1694|Q7694|qid=Q7694}}), flooding of the Karasu River swept away the shrine buildings. The washed-away main hall was recovered, repaired, and rebuilt on a raised foundation.
In {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 11 ({{ill|1698|Q7706|qid=Q7706}}), {{ill|Takeda Nobusada|Q56353014|qid=Q56353014}}, grandson of Kawakubo Nobutoshi, was transferred to {{ill|Tango Province|Q1054331|qid=Q1054331}}.
Kanakubo Castle was abandoned, and the shrine declined. <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒"/>

In {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} 3 ({{ill|1738|Q6996|qid=Q6996}}), the local land steward rebuilt the torii gate and offered rice.
During the {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}} era ({{ill|1848|Q7647|qid=Q7647}}–{{ill|1854|Q7670|qid=Q7670}}), the land steward repaired the shrine buildings and donated sacred rice fields. <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒"/>

In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), the shrine name was restored from “Inari Shrine” to the current “Imaki Aosaka Inami Ikegami Shrine.” <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒"/>

== Events <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒" /> ==
* New Year’s Day Festival (January 2)
* Prayer for a Good Harvest (March 17)
* Great Purification Rite (June 30)
* Sacred Rice Field Festival (July 25)
* Grand Annual Festival (Sunday closest to October 17)
* Harvest Festival (Sunday closest to November 27)
* Great Purification Rite (December 29)

== Access ==
* From JR {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}} {{ill|Jimbohara Station|Q845133|qid=Q845133}}, take the Kamisato Town bus {{ill|Komugicchi-go|Q28682946|qid=Q28682946}} (Northern Route) bound for “Unix.” Get off at “Ikegami Shrine.”
* 25-minute walk (1.9 km) from JR {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}} {{ill|Jimbohara Station|Q845133|qid=Q845133}}
